To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total potential for emission reduction of methane is estimated to be 25 – 50% and that of nitrous oxide is estimated to be less then 10%.

the technical potential for methane reduction is about one third of the present methane emissions, that the technical potential of nitrous oxide reduction is about 10% of the present nitrous oxide emissions, that the economic potential for methane reduction, i.e. the reduction that can be attained at negative emission reduction costs is about half of the technical potential, that the economic nitrous oxide reduction potential is negligible, and that the reduction can be attained over 10 – 15 years.

the technical potential of methane emission reduction is about one third, that the economic potential of methane emission reductions is about half of the technical potential and that the economic potential is attainable over a period of about 10-20 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for the determination of emission reduction potentials and costs of emission reduction technologies.

the identification of technologies for the reduction of non-CO, greenhouse gases, the quantification of the emission reduction potential and the determination of the specific emission reduction cost for these technologies.
the identification and evaluation of technologies to reduce the emission of non-CO 2 greenhouse gases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the potential for reducing methane emissions from the sources mentioned above is considerable.
methane emission reduction techniques can be applied in a cost-effective manner.
the technical potential for reducing methane and nitrous emissions is large, but that the economic potential is less than the technical potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a substantial technical potential for reducing methane and nitrous-oxide emissions.
emission reduction techniques are available for methane and nitous oxide.
the technical potential for emission reductions of both methane and nitrous oxides is considerable, but that this will only be realized when a proper policy framework is established.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many possibilities to reduce non-CO2 GHG emissions.
the potential for reducing non-CO2 GHG emissions is large.
there is a substantial potential for emission reduction of both greenhouse gases.
